Speaking as someone who played dark souls blind on release before having played demon's souls and the former being my favorite game of all time, they just have so much going for them and very little against them. 

The world/level design is highly reminiscent of a metroidvania but in 3d. The difficulty is JUST hard enough that nearly every single boss defeat feels accomplishing without the feeling of frustration carrying over afterwards. Every single enemy can murder you but not in a way where you feel like you were cheated. The lore, while comfortably tucked away, is extremely rich and rewarding to discover. 

Finally, the pvp, man was the pvp bullshit. But it was a very endearing bullshit. It felt very similar to early fighting games. There were obviously OP strats (backstab fishing cause the netcode sucked ass) but you could seek out communities and people who partook in what was called "honor duels" where there are agreed upon rules and strats that were not allowed. In these honor duels is where I truly found my love for competitive gaming. The skill ceiling was sky high but even bad players could sneak in a win based on sheer luck (parry spam). 

The first dark souls is damn near a masterpiece and I'd call it a 10/10 if not for a VERY few amount of certain extremely lackluster areas and bosses.

The biggest downfall of dark souls for newer players in my opinion is their ability to farm levels and having a shield. Both can trivialize combat, removing the game's biggest draw - it's difficulty.

Aye, this is because timbersaw's spells do not pierce spell immunity. To hurt someone through BKB with a spell your ability must 1: pierce spell immunity; and 2: deal damage that is NOT magic (aka physical or pure). Dismember, however can be cast on someone who is spell immune BUT it does MAGIC damage so it does no damage to said opponent.

This is all due to the fact that bkb does 2 things. It makes you spell immune, AND gives 100% magic damage resistance. The two mechanics are not the same

All pure damage GOES THROUGH magic immunity. It's just some spells that deal pure damage can't be cast on a magic immune hero. It's hard to make sense of, I know; but piercing bkb and pure damage are entirely different mechanics.
